content:
nina: Lumen trial reports a sudden spike of 429s during SDK onboarding. They flipped on background prefetch/autosync and saw a big fanout. Can eng take a look?

jamal: Do we know if they're using ephemeral tokens per session or a shared API key? Any client logs?

nina: They're using short-lived tokens from their auth service (1 token per tab). Attaching a snippet from their developer console around the spike: 
```
[2026-03-21T09:12:10.210Z] POST /v1/embeds 200 120ms Authorization: Bearer eph_tok_abc X-Client: lumen-web
[2026-03-21T09:12:11.004Z] POST /v1/embeds 429 8ms Retry-After: 10
[2026-03-21T09:12:11.007Z] POST /v1/embeds 429 9ms Retry-After: 10
[2026-03-21T09:12:11.015Z] POST /v1/embeds 429 10ms Retry-After: 10
```
Multiple tabs refresh tokens at the same time and immediately prefetch vectors.

rachel: Sounds like two problems: token-refresh alignment (many clients hitting the system together) and no client-side concurrency limits. Quick client patches: add randomized offset to refresh, elect a single prefetch leader per user session (localStorage lock), and limit concurrent prefetches per origin.

nina: Any SDK knobs we can suggest that are low-effort for them?

rachel: Yes; recommending these config changes in our JS SDK: 
```
{ 
  prefetch: true,
  prefetch_concurrency: 3,            // default is 8
  prefetch_cooldown_ms: 2500,         // space out bursts
  ephemeral_refresh_jitter_ms: 45000  // randomize refresh across clients
}
```
Also make sure they respect Retry-After on 429s and back off exponentially.

jamal: On infra side, onboarding trials currently share the embed bucket (600/min/token). That model punishes ephemeral-per-tab flows. I'll open infra ticket to add a grace policy for ephemeral tokens and consider tenant-level smoothing for trials. Creating infra-812 now.

ingress-bot: Notice: ap-southeast-2 observed a 9% jump in 429 rate for customer lumen from 2026-03-21T09:11:00 to 2026-03-21T09:13:00.

nina: Good. I'll queue an enablement session with Lumen tomorrow 3pm UTC to run the SDK patch and monitor. I'll share a short rollback snippet (disable prefetch) if they still see errors.

jamal: If they can't patch quickly, temp workaround: serve embeddings from a short-lived cache on their side (client-level LRU) and stagger background workers by random backoff on startup.

rachel: I'll draft the exact JS snippet and a recommended test plan (local repro: open 6 tabs, force token rotate, confirm no >2 concurrent prefetches).

nina: Thanks — please paste the snippet here when ready. I'll update after the call. :rocket:
